body:
Government acting as buyer, seller or grantor rather than as regulator.
Procurement and competitive-bid rules and their exceptions, franchise grants and
reserved rights, municipal utility tariffs and customer contracts, prices the
city sets for things it sells.
Ask: is the city setting terms it will itself trade on, or setting rules others
must follow?

Raises money rather than governing conduct. Occupation and business license
taxes, tax exemptions and credits, bare fee schedules.
Carve-out, ask: does failing to pay stop them operating, or only make them a
debtor? If payment conditions lawful operation, that is an eligibility condition
and the row is CORE at step 4. Only the amount, the exemption and the bare
schedule are revenue.

The effect on commerce runs through the permitted use of land rather than
through a rule on a trade. Permitted-use tables, commercial districts, setbacks,
dimensional standards, mixed-use lists.
Carve-out, ask: does the provision put conditions on the OPERATOR (hours,
customers, signage, registration), or on the PARCEL? A home-occupation or
short-term-rental provision conditioning the operator is CORE. The bare use
table is land-use.

General law that reached step 4 only because it was scoped to licensees or
commercial premises. A sign code applying to all signs in a district, a licensing
division enforcing ordinary traffic law against its licensees, exceptions written
into anti-discrimination law.
Carve-out, ask: is this aimed at COMMERCIAL signage, advertising or false
advertising? If so, CORE. Aimed at all signs, general-law.

The duty falls on someone dealing with a business rather than on the business.
Customer obligations, utility-customer rules, employee conduct provisions written
against the employee. This is the step 3 outcome.

The administrative machinery of a chapter whose commercial subject is
identifiable: how to apply, what the clerk does, hearings, renewal mechanics,
inspection steps.
Guard, ask: can you tell from THIS text what trade the chapter licenses? If not,
that is step 1 and no-context, not procedure.
Boundary with core: when the paperwork duty falls on the business under threat of
sanction - a dealer who must file a daily report - the recordkeeping IS the
regulated conduct, and the row is CORE. procedure is for machinery performed by
the agency.

A definitions section for a chapter whose commercial subject is identifiable.
Split from procedure so the two can be counted separately.

The regulated activity is commercial only sometimes and the text does not say
which. Kennels, day care, massage, towing, assisted living.
Carve-out, ask: does the text name a commercial operator ("massage parlor",
"kennel operator")? If so, CORE.
